blocks.content: Quiz: In the quiz we have
What do questions[i] give us for each value of i?
Tap an option below to answer:
The player's answer for question i.
Incorrect, give it another shot!
The player's answer comes from prompt() and is stored in userAnswer. questions[i] is the data for the question; we compare userAnswer to q.answer from that object.
The player's answer comes from prompt() and is stored in userAnswer. questions[i] is the data for the question; we compare userAnswer to q.answer from that object.
The score after question i.
Incorrect, give it another shot!
The score is stored in the variable score and we update it with score++. questions[i] is the current question data (text, options, correct answer), not the score.
The score is stored in the variable score and we update it with score++. questions[i] is the current question data (text, options, correct answer), not the score.
The question object for the current round - the one with .question, .options, and .answer for that question.
Correct Answer!

Correct. questions[i] is the element at position i in the questions array. Each element is an object with question text, options array, and correct answer - exactly what we need to show the question and check the player's answer.

Correct. questions[i] is the element at position i in the questions array. Each element is an object with question text, options array, and correct answer - exactly what we need to show the question and check the player's answer.
The total number of questions.
Incorrect, give it another shot!
The number of questions is questions.length. questions[i] is one single question object at index i, not the count.
The number of questions is questions.length. questions[i] is one single question object at index i, not the count.
